words.prose: {{ar:ءَأَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:ʾa-antum}}) opens the ayah by making the addressees visible before the action is named. Since {{ar:تَزْرَعُونَهُۥٓ}} ({{tr:tazraʿūnahū}}) already carries second-person plural agreement, the retained independent pronoun is not mere subject identification; it isolates the human agent for scrutiny. The interrogative hamza makes the first beat a live question-form, while the rhetoric makes the human-agency answer collapse. This opening also prepares the exclusive turn through {{ar:أَمْ نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:am naḥnu}}), so the question becomes a binary agency trial rather than a neutral description of farming. In the surrounding challenge series, the same kind of pronoun-fronted questioning dismantles human claims over generation (56:58-59), crops (56:63-64), water (56:68-69), and fire (56:71-72).

topics.reason: The verb already marks second-person plural subject agreement, so the independent pronoun's fronted retention gives the human agent separate prominence before the verbal predicate.

topics.headline: opening sets the binary agency test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the opening word as the crop-domain member of a repeated challenge series, where human activity is narrowed into a direct human-versus-divine agency test.
topics.reason: The opening pronoun is structurally answered by the later divine pronoun through the disjunctive particle, and the row evidence places this in the repeated challenge pattern spanning 56:58-72, including the water parallel in 56:68-69 and fire parallel in 56:72.

words.prose: {{ar:تَزْرَعُونَهُۥٓ}} ({{tr:tazraʿūnahū}}) carries the earlier cultivated object forward: the attached suffix points back to what was being plowed in 56:63, so the question is about what happens to that same object after human labor. The imperfect verb presents the human side as an ongoing, contingent act rather than a completed possession of the result. Lexically, {{ar:ز ر ع}} ({{tr:z-r-ʿ}}) lets sowing, cultivation, crop, and growth-causing press into one verbal slot; the point is not that every dictionary branch is active, but that this form can expose the gap between placing or tending seed and causing living growth. This finite human-facing verb also stands out against a root field dominated by crop nouns and nominal forms, concentrating the agency problem in the verbal slot. That pressure is sharpened because the same root returns in {{ar:ٱلزَّٰرِعُونَ}} ({{tr:al-zāriʿūna}}): the ayah repeats the root while changing agent, form, and clause type. The repeated z-r-ʿ sound sequence binds the two halves, and its movement from sibilant through liquid into pharyngeal depth reinforces the shift from visible surface action toward hidden growth. The root also belongs to the crop imagery seen in 48:29, but here it is the crop-domain member of the agency challenges across 56:58-72.

words.prose: {{ar:أَمْ}} ({{tr:am}}) is the hinge of the ayah. Its connected-disjunction force depends on the opening interrogative in {{ar:ءَأَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:ʾa-antum}}), so it does not act as a loose English-style or; it stretches one question across two completed agency claims. The particle keeps the first clause from collapsing into the second, while its rhetorical pressure leans toward correction: not the human claim, but {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}) as the answering side. Because it stands alone with no attached pronoun or verb, the whole relation between the clauses is carried by this small pivot. Its closed final sound also marks a compact stop, then a nasal bridge into the opening of the divine pronoun.

topics.headline: connected disjunction carries one question across two clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle links the two halves under one question and requires a resolution between named agents.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence identifies the second member as the coordinated alternative to the first, matching the connected-disjunction reading after the opening interrogative.

topics.headline: corrective reading sharpens but does not replace the binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the second half as more than a neutral option; it corrects the human-agency claim while the local grammar still stages a binary question.
topics.reason: The local syntax strongly licenses connected disjunction, so the disconnected or corrective value survives as rhetorical pressure rather than as a replacement parse.

topics.headline: central particle excludes a shared-agency middle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah turn at this word from challenged human action to asserted divine identity, with no unmarked both-and answer on the surface.
topics.reason: The particle links two completed alternatives and occupies the middle position between the human verbal clause and the divine nominal clause, preserving opposed clause-units.

words.prose: {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}) makes the divine speaker explicit before the title arrives. The predicate could not be left as an abstract grower-class; the pronoun fixes who is being identified and places that speaker directly opposite {{ar:ءَأَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:ʾa-antum}}). As the subject of a nominal clause, it changes the answer from a competing action into a standing identity claim: not simply someone grows, but We are the ones named by the following predicate. Its independent form also matters; the speaker is not hidden in an ending but stands visibly at the start of the divine half. Across {{ar:أَمْ}} ({{tr:am}}), the two pronouns form the ayah's agency axis, and their shared nasal sounds audibly frame the opposed agents without softening the contrast.

topics.reason: The pronoun is an independent form, and the sound/boundary rows reinforce the same local transition from challenged human action to explicit divine speaker.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلزَّٰرِعُونَ}} ({{tr:al-zāriʿūna}}) is where the ayah lands. The definite article, masculine plural nominative agreement, and predicate role bind the participle to {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}), so the phrase is not an indefinite description of growers but a title-like claim: We are the growers. In this divine predicate, the crop root is narrowed toward causing growth and germination, not merely performing the mechanical act of sowing. The active participle also changes the grammar of the dispute: the human side used the finite verb {{ar:تَزْرَعُونَهُۥٓ}} ({{tr:tazraʿūnahū}}), while the divine side uses a durable participial identity. That participial choice is distributionally marked against the root's more common crop nouns and gerunds, so the final title is not just another root occurrence. The same root therefore frames the ayah, but the form and agent are reversed. As the final word, the participle closes the binary question by turning the agricultural field into a settled divine agency-title, with the assimilated definite opening and doubled z-sound adding audible weight to the closure.

topics.headline: definite participle lands as a title-like predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word identifies the divine speaker by a definite predicate-title rather than offering an indefinite farmer description.
topics.reason: The word is a definite masculine plural active participle functioning as predicate of the divine pronoun, and the binary question gives that definiteness restrictive force.

topics.headline: divine predicate selects growth-causing agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the final title assigns the hidden causation of growth to the divine speaker, while ordinary agricultural branches remain outside the selected local sense.
topics.reason: The root's accepted crop/growth branch supports the divine growth-causer payoff, while local predication to the divine speaker limits the sense away from ordinary mechanical sowing and unrelated root branches.

topics.headline: active participle makes agency durable and marked
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah chooses a rare active-participle form for divine growth-agency where a finite verb or crop noun could have continued the field.
topics.reason: The contextual profile marks the active participle as low occurrence and concentrated here, and the local form is a participial predicate rather than a finite verb.

topics.headline: final participle answers the opening root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same crop root bookend the ayah while the grammar shifts from human doing to divine being.
topics.reason: The final word is the last predicate of the ayah and reprises the same root used in the human verb, but with a new agent and participial form.

topics.headline: assimilated definite opening gives closure weight

topics.reason: The definite article is visibly part of the word, and the assimilation/sound rows reinforce the same final title already established by grammar.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Cultivation is separated from actual growth.** Repeated `ز ر ع` activates **B001**, growing and cultivating crops. The disjunction assigns apparently shared lexical action to rival agents, forcing a distinction between placing seed and causing growth. **Abductive move:** I infer that humans perform the preparatory sense while the speaker claims effective growth. **Reading change:** one verb is split into instrumental and originating roles.

2. **Agricultural dealing cannot purchase the yield.** `ز ر ع` **B003** supplies sharecropping or agricultural dealing. **Abductive move:** I infer that ownership arrangements regulate labor and shares but cannot contractually compel germination. **Reading change:** the question also limits economic control over the crop.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The cloud-descent contrast at 56:69 supplied an exact structural analogue: receiving or handling an output differs from causing its decisive transition.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The repeated grower-root separates preparing a cause from making growth occur.** Finite verb and agent noun repeat `ز ر ع` (B001, growing and cultivating crops) across the same “you or We” contrast used in ayah 59. Ayah 63 has named human tilling; ayat 65–69 show that the crop can become debris and that water likewise descends from beyond human control. The packet’s branch spans sowing and growth, but the local alternation assigns *ḥarth* to the audience before reserving the decisive *zāriʿ* role; I infer a contextual sharpening from cultivation to effective germination. Human action is real without being self-sufficient.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 56:69 assigns water’s descent beyond human agency and 56:72 does the same for the tree’s origination, confirming that growth sits inside a network of prior means no cultivator authors.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Embodied life is a measured production whose material, duration, form, and replacement remain under an agency beyond its human transmitters.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Measuring leather before cutting, reproductive seed, visible pregnancy, and substitution of forms make creation legible as calibrated manufacture without reducing it to mechanism alone.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Human seed and agricultural seed share a generative frame
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Semen functions as seed, descends as reproductive fluid, begins pregnancy, and becomes visible in the body.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: male seed as crop seed `quranic:root_000630:B004/m01`; seminal material `quranic:root_001450:B002/m01`; emitted male fluid `quranic:root_001492:B009/m01`; onset of pregnancy `quranic:root_001502:B009/m01`; visible signs of pregnancy `quranic:root_000531:B010/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The lexical field explicitly joins the reproductive and agricultural demonstrations. Seed is cast in both womb and soil, pregnancy is the hidden onset of growth, and visible enlargement is the point at which an unseen generative process declares itself.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P4 Provision Chains Humans Use but Do Not Originate
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Food, water, and fire arrive through multi-stage transformations that humans initiate or use locally but cannot secure at the level of growth, descent, or latent energy.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Debt, famine, cloud husbandry, minimal-input flourishing, tinder, and traveler supplies expose the operational dependencies inside ordinary provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Field labor can terminate in harvest or ruin
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Seed is cast into worked ground and grown, but the crop can be broken into dry fragments, converting expected gain into persistent loss and deprivation.

identity_judgment.rationale: Verilen çerçeve, bitkiyi yetiştirip geliştirme merkezini doğru yakalar; ancak kaynak ifadesi bununla sınırlı değildir. Tohumu toprağa atma, yetişen ekin, ekim yeri, saçılmış tanelerden kendiliğinden çıkma, bitkinin ekin verir hale gelmesi ve çocuğun yetişmesine ilişkin benzetmeli kullanım da aynı dalda yer alır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği yetiştirme ve gelişmedir; ekme eylemi, yetişen ürün, yer adları ve benzetmeli kullanımlar bu çekirdeğe bağlı fakat birbirinden ayrı yüzlerdir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın yetiştirme ve ekme anlamlarını kapsarken yalnız belirli kalıplarda görülen çocuk yetiştirme, ekin verir hale gelme ve bitmeme anlamlarını ayrı yüzler olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi, özellikle bitkiyi, gelişip olgunluğuna ulaşıncaya kadar büyütme; tarımsal bağlamda tohumu toprağa atma, bundan çıkan ekini ve ekim yerini adlandırma alanıdır. Ayrıca saçılmış tanelerden kendiliğinden çıkan bitkiyi, bitkinin ekin verir hale gelmesini ve benzetme yoluyla çocuğun yetişip olgunlaşmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, bir canlıyı geliştirip olgunlaşacağı son aşamaya kadar yetiştirmektir.
Tarımsal uygulamada bu süreç, tohumu toprağa atarak yetişmesini başlatmayı bildirir.
Süreç adı, yetiştirilen bitkiye ve özellikle tahıl ekinine sonuç adı olarak aktarılır.
Eylem alanı, ekim yapılan yeri ve ekili alanları adlandıracak biçimde genişler.
Hasat sırasında saçılan tanelerden daha sonra kendiliğinden çıkan bitki özel bir gerçekleşme olarak bu alana girer.
Çocuğun büyütülüp gençliğinin olgunluğuna erişmesi, bitkinin yetişmesine benzetilerek anlatılır.
Bitkinin ekin oluşturur ya da ekin taşır duruma gelmesi belirli bir kalıpla ifade edilir.
